plan.why: The three departments with the largest dollar gaps are Stationery ($34,988), Snacks & Beverages ($17,446), and Electronics ($15,397), so the searches target back-to-school demand, Walmart's quarterly commentary on electronics, and New York's economy, fuel prices and weather that week.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

BENTONVILLE, Ark., Nov. 15, 2012 — Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. (NYSE: WMT) today reported financial results for the quarter ended Oct. 31, 2012. Net sales for the third quarter of fiscal 2013 were $113.2 billion, an increase of 3.4 percent from $109.5 billion in the third quarter last year. Net sales for this quarter included a negative currency exchange rate impact of approximately $1.7 billion. Without the currency impact, net sales would have been $114.9 billion. Membership and other income increased 2.1 percent to $725 million. Total revenue was $113.9 billion, an increase of 3.4 percent from last year. See additional information at the end of this release regarding non-GAAP measures.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: So, let's get on to our results. Mike Duke will kick off the news for the third quarter. M
passages.text: Walmart U.S. posted a comp sales increase of 1.5 percent, and delivered approximately $2.3 billion in net sales growth. Back to school activities drove sales early in the quarter, and the mid-September launch of layaway was important in helping customers. Operating income outpaced net sales growth for the quarter and was a key driver of our overall company profit. Bill and his team are executing very innovative plans to drive traffic and to help America's families have a great holiday season. That's what our customers expect and we will deliver. We announced our extended Black Friday program, and customers are already working on their shopping lists.

We discuss our existing FCPA investigation and related matters in the filed portion of our Nov. 15, 2012 Form 8-K, as well as in our Form 10-Q filed on Sept. 6, 2012 and investors are referred to those SEC reports for information concerning those matters. The forward-looking statements made in this release are made only as of the date of this release, and Walmart undertakes no obligation to update them to reflect subsequent events or circumstances. Wal-Mart Stores, Inc.

Consumer Spending Retailers report that sales activity has remained flat in recent weeks. A major retail chain reports that sales in the region were sluggish in August and especially in September, running well below comparable 2011 levels. Some of the weakness is attributed to unseasonably mild weather, which dampened sales of seasonal merchandise. A major mall in upstate New York describes sales activity as "stagnant", with sales flat to down slightly from a year ago in August and September. The pricing environment is described as quite promotional, and acquisition costs of goods are characterized as mostly stable to declining modestly. Auto dealers in upstate New York report steady sales activity. New vehicle sales were up 6-9 percent from a year earlier in August but are projected to be flat to up slightly in September. Sales of used cars have been mixed since the last report, while dealers' service departments note some slowing in business. Wholesale and retail credit conditions remain favorable.

report.summary: The same departments were below the ML forecast at most other Walmart stores and across the New York stores that week, so part of the pattern looks wider than this store. Store 27 fell further than the chain as a whole, which points to possible local factors that the data provided cannot confirm. Some of the outside context, such as cooler weather, may also fit the seasonal drops, but no report covers this specific week.

findings.title: Same departments fell at most other stores
findings.text: In Dept 3 Stationery, 43 of 44 other stores were below the ML forecast that week, and in Dept 16 Lawn & Garden, 42 of 44 were. This suggests a shared cause across stores, such as category demand or calendar timing, though this has not been verified.

findings.title: Chain-wide sales were also below forecast
findings.text: All 45 stores together were at $44,169,616 against a $46,628,419 forecast (-5.3%), and 36 of 45 stores were below the forecast. The week is therefore a softer one across the chain, not only at this store.

findings.title: Store 27 fell further than the chain
findings.text: Store 27 was at $1,511,915 against a $1,751,935 forecast (-13.7%), and 60 of its 69 departments were below forecast. Markdowns of $23,812 were recorded for the whole store that week but cannot be tied to any department, so they do not explain the department gaps.

findings.title: Electronics drop is specific to this store
findings.text: In Dept 72 Electronics, the other New York stores were at or above the ML forecast (Store 24 +0.1%; Store 19 +2.4%; Store 15 +18.2%), and across all stores the department was +0.3%. This store's -28.4% gap is therefore unusual and may point to a local cause such as stock, pricing or displays.

findings.title: Cooler weather and report on seasonal sales
findings.text: Temperature this week was 69°F against 76°F in the prior four-week median, and local fuel was $4.09/gal against $4.01. A Fed report from Oct 10, 2012 said "Some of the weakness is attributed to unseasonably mild weather, which dampened sales of seasonal merchandise." That report describes New York sales in August and September, not this week, so it offers only general context for the Lawn & Garden gap.

departments.what_supports_it: This was the largest percentage gap at -59.2%, and 43 of 44 other stores and all 3 New York stores were also below forecast, so the drop is widespread rather than local.
This had the largest dollar gap at $17,446 (-14.0%), but the chain-wide drop was small (-6.2% overall), so most of this gap sits at this store.
This gap of -28.4% appears only here; other New York stores were at or above forecast, so this is the clearest store-specific candidate.
Forty of 44 other stores and all 3 New York stores were below forecast, with a chain-wide median of -6.9%, pointing to a broad drop in this category.
The drop was -44.6%, with 42 of 44 other stores and all 3 New York stores below forecast, and the Oct 10 report links seasonal weakness to mild weather in the region.
This gap was small (-4.4%) and close to the chain-wide median of -0.9%, so it is a minor part of the store's total gap.

report.not_found: I looked for a local event, a stock or delivery problem, a staffing change, a competitor action or a report covering this specific week, and found none in the data provided.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

Consumer Spending Consumer spending slowed modestly and contacts were less optimistic about future sales in the months ahead. Retail sales declined slightly from the previous survey, but remained above year-ago levels. Several contacts cited political uncertainty and rising gasoline prices as key reasons for the slowdown. Expectations for future sales also eased somewhat, while store inventories were largely unchanged. Growth in auto sales was less robust than previous months, and expectations for future sales weakened slightly. However, several auto dealers in Oklahoma noted higher sales due to strong energy activity in their areas. Contacts said sales were strongest for mid-sized family sedans and crossover SUVs, while sales of full-size trucks and SUVs remained weak.

passages.text: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms BENTONVILLE, Ark., July 18, 2012 /PRNewswire/ -- Walmart today announced the results of the "Walmart Class of 2012 Back-to-School Survey," which revealed that 76 percent of moms with children in kindergarten to 12th grade consider back-to-school a time for a fresh start over Jan. 1[1] – in fact, nine out of ten moms make back-to-school "resolutions" in preparation for the year ahead[2]. With 78 percent of moms planning to get organized[3] this new school year, Walmart today launched Classrooms by Walmart, an online compilation of thousands of classroom supply lists representing schools in all 50 states plus Washington, D.C., making it easier for moms to get their back-to-school supplies online and in Walmart stores.

In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

Retail and Tourism First District retailers contacted for this round indicate that sales through mid to late September are slightly above 2011. Year-over-year sales increases in recent months range from low single-digit to high single-digit percentage gains, although one retailer reports that its 2012 sales to date are 2 percent to 3 percent below last year's. Furniture sales have picked up after declining during the summer, while spending on apparel and household items remains strong. Contacts express some concern that consumer sentiment could be negatively affected by domestic politics and the fiscal cliff, which increases their uncertainty about how well the end-of-year 2012 holiday sales season will turn out. While such concerns lead retailers to expect the U.S. economy will remain flat over the next 6 to 8 months, respondents are nonetheless cautiously optimistic that their 2012 revenues will end up slightly ahead of 2011 levels.

report.summary: Store 23 was below the ML forecast in 48 of 67 departments for the week ending Sep 7, 2012, and the store as a whole was $1,426,508 against a $1,597,271 forecast (-10.7%). Many of the largest gaps are in departments where the other New England stores also fell below the forecast, while Walmart overall was close to its forecast that week. Possible reasons are listed below, but none is verified.

findings.title: Walmart overall was close to forecast
findings.text: Across all 45 stores that week, sales were $48,296,614 against a $48,462,259 forecast (-0.3%), and 28 of 45 stores were below the forecast. A nationwide drop does not explain the size of Store 23's gaps.

findings.title: Stationery and apparel fell at many stores
findings.text: Dept 3 Stationery was below the ML forecast at 36 of 44 other stores (median -44.1%), and Dept 31 Accessories at 35 of 43 (median -39.9%). Dept 24 Boyswear and Dept 33 Girlswear also fell at most other stores, so this store's drops in these departments are part of a wider pattern.

findings.title: New England stores fell together in many departments
findings.text: All five other New England stores were below the ML forecast in Dept 3, Dept 31, Dept 24, Dept 33, Dept 11, Dept 14, Dept 46, Dept 9 and Dept 23. The regional pattern suggests a shared cause such as local demand, though the data alone does not show which one.

findings.title: Some drops are specific to this store
findings.text: Dept 72 Electronics (-23.3%), Dept 17 Home Furnishings / Decor (-25.3%) and Dept 11 Hardware (-26.2%) were well below the ML forecast here, while the same departments were close to flat across other stores (medians +0.2%, +1.6% and +0.3%). This points toward something local, such as stock, staffing or displays, rather than a company-wide change.

findings.title: Boston district reports mixed on apparel and furniture
findings.text: A Boston Fed report dated Aug 29, 2012 said that "Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment." A Boston Fed report dated Oct 10, 2012 (after this week) said "spending on apparel and household items remains strong" and that "Furniture sales have picked up after declining during the summer." These are district-wide statements, not this store's results, and the later report does not describe Labor Day week.

Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. passages.section: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms
passages.text: "For the moms who shop our stores, back-to-school isn't just about checking items off their lists. It's about a fresh start, changing routines and getting children ready with products that match their personalities and budgets," said Duncan Mac Naughton, chief merchandising officer, Walmart U.S. "We're committed to setting our customers up for success this back-to-school season by sticking to our plan – offering everyday low prices and the broadest assortment of the right merchandise their families need." The "Walmart Class of 2012 Back-to-School Survey" also revealed that saving money and eating healthier topped moms' "new school year" resolutions, and uncovered moms' most important purchases for the season:

EX-99.1 d440140dex991.htm PRESS RELEASE Press Release Exhibit 99.1 For Immediate Release Media Relations Contact Randy Hargrove 800-331-0085 Investor Relations Contact Carol Schumacher 479-277-1498 Pre-recorded conference call 877-523-5612 (U.S. and Canada) 201-689-8483 (All other countries) Call passcode: 9256278 Walmart reports Q3 EPS of $1.08, reaffirms top end of full-year EPS guidance; Company is well positioned for Q4 holidays Q3 Highlights : Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. (Walmart) reported third quarter diluted earnings per share from continuing operations of $1.08, within guidance of $1.04 to $1.09. This was an 11.3 percent increase from the $0.97 per share reported for the third quarter last year.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Retail Sales Retail sales grew slightly over the reporting period and were up from a year ago. Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel. Sales growth in the Eleventh District remained stronger than the nation, on average, according to two large retailers. Retailers expect a seasonal pickup in demand in the fourth quarter, although sales will likely be down from last year. Automobile sales were mostly flat since the last report, but were up from year ago levels. Inventories were lighter than desired. Contacts said political uncertainty was hampering consumer confidence, and outlooks were cautious.

passages.section: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms
passages.text: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms BENTONVILLE, Ark., July 18, 2012 /PRNewswire/ -- Walmart today announced the results of the "Walmart Class of 2012 Back-to-School Survey," which revealed that 76 percent of moms with children in kindergarten to 12th grade consider back-to-school a time for a fresh start over Jan. 1[1] – in fact, nine out of ten moms make back-to-school "resolutions" in preparation for the year ahead[2]. With 78 percent of moms planning to get organized[3] this new school year, Walmart today launched Classrooms by Walmart, an online compilation of thousands of classroom supply lists representing schools in all 50 states plus Washington, D.C., making it easier for moms to get their back-to-school supplies online and in Walmart stores.

passages.text: Consumer Spending Retailers report that sales activity has firmed somewhat since the last report. Two major retail chains report that sales in the region were on plan in July and ahead of plan in early August. Similarly a major retail mall in upstate New York reports some firming in sales, as well as shopper traffic, in July and early August, following lackluster business in May and June. Retail prices continue to be described as steady--including apparel prices, which had previously been expected to drift down with the retreat in cotton prices earlier this year. Stores in New York City have performed on par or modestly better than those in the rest of the region. Inventories are generally said to be at or slightly above desired levels.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Consumer Spending Retailers report that sales activity has been somewhat softer since the last report. One major retail chain indicates that sales were down noticeably from a year earlier, with home goods sales especially weak. Another major chain reports that sales slowed in June and were running somewhat below plan but still up marginally from a year earlier; however, some improvement was noted during the first few days of July. Retail contacts in upstate New York report that sales were mixed in May but picked up in June, again buoyed by Canadian shoppers. Retail prices continue to be described as steady. Inventories are generally said to be at or slightly above desired levels.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported modest increases in retail spending on a year-over-year basis, but many reported slower growth in recent months compared with earlier in the year; however, Boston and Cleveland reported sales as flat, and New York cited softer sales. There were a few reports that high summer temperatures negatively affected sales. Sales of big-ticket household goods were strong in the Richmond, Chicago, Kansas City, and Dallas Districts, while sales were reportedly flat for home furnishings and major appliances in the San Francisco District. Boston reported that sales for furniture and electronics had slowed, and retailers in the New York District reported that home goods sales were weak. Reports from luxury-goods retailers were mixed.

During the 13-week period, both comp ticket and traffic rose for Walmart U.S., and both grocery and general merchandise had positive comp sales. "Our comp sales momentum continued through the second quarter, with July being one of our strongest months. All three geographic business units and all store formats had positive comp sales. Customers are responding to our continued focus on providing the right assortment at everyday low prices and are shopping the entire store," said Bill Simon, Walmart U.S. president and chief executive officer. "We have a powerful strategy and I'm confident in our ability to deliver sustained strong financial performance." For the 4-5-4 period from July 28 through October 26, Walmart U.S. expects comparable store sales to range from 1.0 percent to 3.0 percent.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: In consumables, sales remained strong as our continued focus on price and assortment drove positive traffic. For the third consecutive quarter, all departments reported positive comps as customers responded favorably to product innovation and value-driven pricing.

report.summary: Store 27 is flagged for 21 departments that are below the ML forecast, with a total gap of $122,841 (an ML estimate, not a verified loss). Most stores and all three other New York State stores in the same departments were also below the ML forecast that week, and the store's overall drop (-9.2%) was larger than Walmart's (-5.0%). The available reports are general and do not point to a cause at this store.

findings.title: Same departments down at most stores
findings.text: In Dept 95 DSD Grocery, Snacks & Beverages, all three other New York State stores were also below the ML forecast that week, as were 39 of 44 other stores overall. The same pattern appears in Dept 11 Hardware and Dept 91 Frozen Food, which suggests a shared cause rather than one specific to this store.

findings.title: Store-wide gap larger than Walmart's
findings.text: Across the store, 61 of 68 departments were below the ML forecast, and the store as a whole was -9.2% below its forecast. Walmart overall that week was -5.0% below its forecast, so this store fell further than the chain, which points to something that may be local.

findings.title: Regional report: home goods weak
findings.text: The Fed's Jul 18, 2012 report says "retailers in the New York District reported that home goods sales were weak" (P4). This is a New York District observation from before the week ending Jul 27, 2012, and it does not describe this store. It may relate to Dept 11 Hardware and Dept 16 Lawn & Garden, but no report links it to this week.

findings.title: Walmart-wide sales were positive
findings.text: Walmart's Aug 16, 2012 earnings release says "July being one of our strongest months," and its quarter comparable sales were +2.2%. The chain as a whole was doing well in this period, even though this store and most of its flagged departments were below the ML forecast.

findings.title: Outside factors show little change
findings.text: No holiday fell in the week. Fuel was $3.82/gal against $3.68 before, temperature was 76°F against 79°F, and unemployment was 8.2%, unchanged. These factors are possible contributors, but the report does not link them to this store's departments.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Now, the remainder of our discussion today is focused on our core business which excludes fuel for comparative purposes, unless otherwise noted.Net sales were $12.2 billion, up 3.6 percent from last year. Our strongest divisional performance was in the West, with our strongest regional performance in the Great Plains, Mid South, and Mid Atlantic. Now I'd like to turn your attention to merchandising. There were three major themes during the third quarter: price investment, moderation of inflation, and new product introduction.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

(Walmart) reported third quarter diluted earnings per share from continuing operations of $1.08, within guidance of $1.04 to $1.09. This was an 11.3 percent increase from the $0.97 per share reported for the third quarter last year.

These reclassifications did not impact the Company's consolidated operating income or net income. Additionally, certain prior period segment asset and expense allocations have been reclassified among segments to be comparable with the current period presentation. The Retail Industry We operate in the highly competitive retail industry in all of the countries we serve. We face strong sales competition from other discount, department, drug, dollar, variety and specialty stores, warehouse clubs and supermarkets. Many of these competitors are national, regional or international chains, as well as internet-based retailers and catalog businesses.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Consumer Spending Retailers report that sales activity has firmed somewhat since the last report. Two major retail chains report that sales in the region were on plan in July and ahead of plan in early August. Similarly a major retail mall in upstate New York reports some firming in sales, as well as shopper traffic, in July and early August, following lackluster business in May and June. Retail prices continue to be described as steady--including apparel prices, which had previously been expected to drift down with the retreat in cotton prices earlier this year. Stores in New York City have performed on par or modestly better than those in the rest of the region. Inventories are generally said to be at or slightly above desired levels.

report.summary: Store 14's flagged departments were below the ML forecast on Sep 14, 2012, and most of them were also below the forecast at other stores and at the other Central Atlantic stores that week. The store as a whole was below forecast by a larger share than Walmart overall, and the cause at this store is not confirmed. The drop looks mostly shared across stores and the region, with a few departments that look more local.

findings.title: Walmart overall was below forecast
findings.text: Across all 45 stores that week, sales were $44,169,616 against a $46,628,419 forecast, which is -5.3%. Thirty-six of 45 stores were below the forecast.

findings.title: Same departments down at most stores
findings.text: Dept 3 Stationery was below the forecast at 43 of 44 other stores, and Dept 16 Lawn & Garden at 42 of 44. Dept 74 Home Management / Storage was below at 42 of 44 other stores, and Dept 31 Accessories at 31 of 43. This points to a drop shared across many stores rather than one store's problem.

findings.title: Central Atlantic stores down together
findings.text: In the Central Atlantic region, all four other stores were below the forecast in Dept 3 Stationery, Dept 11 Hardware, Dept 31 Accessories, Dept 33 Girlswear, Dept 74 Home Management / Storage, Dept 16 Lawn & Garden and Dept 20 Domestics / Bath. A shared regional pattern is a possible sign of a wider cause such as local demand or a regional calendar effect. This is not confirmed.

findings.title: Store-wide gap larger; Dept 40 mostly flat
findings.text: Store 14 as a whole was $1,553,718 against a $1,713,396 forecast, which is -9.3%, and 55 of 68 departments were below forecast. Dept 40 OTC Pharmacy was flat at other stores in the region and across the chain, so its drop may be more local to this store.

findings.title: Cooler weather and fuel prices that week
findings.text: The temperature was 68°F against 75°F in the median of the 4 weeks before, and local fuel was $3.95/gal against $3.85. There was no holiday that week and unemployment was unchanged at 8.7%. These are general conditions that could affect seasonal categories such as Dept 16 Lawn & Garden, but no direct link was found in the data.

findings.title: Regional reports point the other way
findings.text: The Aug 29, 2012 Beige Book said "Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales" before this week. A later Beige Book dated Oct 10, 2012 said "sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts," but it is dated after the week. Neither report names Store 14 or these departments.

departments.what_supports_it: Actual sales were $31,322 against a $59,769 ML forecast, and 43 of 44 other stores were also below forecast that week. All four other Central Atlantic stores were below too, which points to a broad drop.

Actual sales were $2,555 against an $8,315 ML forecast, the largest percentage drop in the list. All four other Central Atlantic stores were below forecast, so it is a shared drop, but the small base makes the percentage less stable.

Some flagged grocery departments, such as Dept 79 Infant Consumables and Dept 92 Dry Grocery, were also below forecast at most other stores and at every other West Coast store, which points to a wider cause. Other drops, such as Dept 3 Stationery and Dept 2 Health & Beauty Aids, appear mostly limited to this store.

findings.title: Grocery drops shared across stores and region
findings.text: Dept 79 Infant Consumables was below the ML forecast at 37 of 44 other stores, and Dept 92 Dry Grocery at 31 of 44. All 5 other West Coast stores were also below the ML forecast in both departments.

findings.title: Grocery softness reported in San Francisco district
findings.text: A Fed report dated Oct 10, 2012 said: "At grocery stores, consumer spending was soft as shoppers continued to shift their purchasing decisions in favor of cheaper products." This is a district-wide statement, not a finding about Store 10.

findings.title: Store 10 below forecast across most departments
findings.text: Store 10 was below the ML forecast in 55 of 68 departments, with $1,649,822 against a forecast of $1,806,634 (-8.7%). Walmart overall that week was $47,131,887 against $48,409,634 (-2.6%), with 35 of 45 stores below forecast.

findings.title: Dept 3 and Dept 2 weak mainly at this store
findings.text: Dept 3 Stationery was -39.0% below the ML forecast here, while 14 of 44 other stores were below forecast in that department. Dept 2 Health & Beauty Aids was -13.0% here, while the median for other stores was -0.2%.

findings.title: Outside factors changed little that week
findings.text: There was no holiday that week. Fuel was $3.89/gal vs $3.91, temperature was 87°F vs 87°F, and unemployment was 7.2% vs 7.2% (compared with the median of the 4 weeks before).

departments.what_supports_it: This was the largest gap in dollars: $27,278 actual against $44,713 forecast (-39.0%). Only 14 of 44 other stores were below forecast in this department, so the drop looks specific to this store.
Actual was $96,348 against $112,432 forecast (-14.3%). Most other stores were not below forecast in this department (18 of 41), so this is mainly a store-level pattern.
Store 10 was -13.0% below forecast, the lowest of 45 stores, while the median for other stores was -0.2%. This drop is specific to this store.
Actual was $31,058 against $42,616 forecast (-27.1%). It was below forecast at 37 of 44 other stores and at all 5 other West Coast stores, so a wider cause is possible.
Actual was $54,525 against $64,910 forecast (-16.0%). It was below forecast at 27 of 40 other stores, and Store 38 was -38.9%, so this is partly shared with other stores.

report.not_found: I looked for a store-specific stock, staffing or pricing record and for holiday, fuel or weather changes that would explain the drops, and found none in the data provided.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: We had positive comps across all geographies and store formats. During the quarter, we focused on being the destination for back-to-school and Halloween shopping. Our merchants and operators developed a strong cross-functional plan, and I'm pleased with our execution and the sales growth achieved this year. As a reminder, a slightly larger portion of Halloween sales versus last year will fall into the fourth quarter comp period, given how the 4-5-4 calendar falls this year.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Doug is up next with an International update. Doug…
passages.text: Let me go through the numbers on a constant currency basis. First, third quarter net sales would have been up 7.6 percent to $34.8 billion. Our Latin American markets made the strongest contribution to our net sales growth, with all countries in the region delivering positive comp sales. Overall, third quarter comp store sales increased in four of our six largest markets. In general, we're delivering healthy average ticket increases, but comparable store traffic remains a concern and it declined in the third quarter in our major markets. We're focused on improving our customer communications in all of our markets, but we're especially focused on the markets where consumer spending is under the most pressure, such as in Japan and the U.K.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

These forward-looking statements are subject to risks, uncertainties and other factors, domestically and internationally, including: general economic conditions; economic conditions affecting specific markets in which we operate; competitive pressures; inflation and deflation; consumer confidence, disposable income, credit availability, spending patterns and debt levels; the seasonality of Walmart's business and seasonal buying patterns in the United States and other markets; geo-political conditions and events; weather conditions and events and their effects; catastrophic events and natural disasters and their effects on Walmart's business; public health emergencies; civil unrest and disturbances and terrorist attacks; commodity prices; the cost of goods Walmart sells; transportation costs; the cost of diesel fuel, gasoline, natural gas and electricity; the selling prices of gasoline; disruption of Walmart's supply chain, including transport of goods from foreign suppliers; trade restrictions; changes in tariff and freight rates; labor costs; changes in employment laws and regulations; the cost of healthcare and other benefits; casualty and other insurance costs; accident-related costs; adoption of or changes in tax and other laws and regulations that affect Walmart's business, including changes in corporate tax rates; developments in, and the outcome of, legal and regulatory proceedings to which Walmart is a party or is subject; currency exchange rate fluctuations; changes in market interest rates; conditions and events affecting domestic and global financial and capital markets; and other risks.

Retail Sales Retail sales grew slightly over the reporting period and were up from a year ago. Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel. Sales growth in the Eleventh District remained stronger than the nation, on average, according to two large retailers. Retailers expect a seasonal pickup in demand in the fourth quarter, although sales will likely be down from last year. Automobile sales were mostly flat since the last report, but were up from year ago levels. Inventories were lighter than desired. Contacts said political uncertainty was hampering consumer confidence, and outlooks were cautious.

report.summary: Store 39 was below the ML forecast in most departments in the week ending Sep 14, 2012, and the same departments were also below forecast at many other stores in Texas and across the chain. The largest gap, Stationery, was below forecast at 43 of 44 other stores. Pharmacy (Rx) is the main exception: it was far below forecast here while most other stores were above theirs, which points to something local. No specific cause has been verified.

findings.title: Stationery and other categories low across stores
findings.text: Stationery was below the ML forecast at 43 of 44 other stores that week, and at all 13 other Texas stores. Lawn & Garden and Household Chemicals show the same pattern across stores. This suggests a wider category or calendar effect, not only a problem at Store 39.

findings.title: Pharmacy gap is specific to this store
findings.text: Pharmacy (Rx) was $6,914 (-15.0%) below the ML forecast here, the lowest of 45 stores. Most other stores were above their forecast in this department that week (median +4.4%). This gap is not explained by a store-wide pattern, so local stock, staffing or data entry are worth checking.

findings.title: Store well below forecast, with most departments low
findings.text: Store 39 was $1,447,604 against a $1,603,182 forecast (-9.7%), with 60 of 68 departments below forecast. The Walmart total for the same week was -5.3%, so this store fell further than the chain overall.

findings.title: Week was soft chain-wide, with no holiday
findings.text: 36 of 45 stores were below forecast that week, and the Walmart total was -5.3% against a forecast of $46,628,419. The week had no holiday, the local fuel price was higher, and the temperature was lower than the four weeks before. These are possible background factors only.

findings.title: Dallas Fed report notes lighter inventories
findings.text: The Dallas Fed Beige Book of Aug 29, 2012, covers the whole district, not this store, and was published before this week. It reports that "Retail sales grew slightly over the reporting period" and that "Inventories were lighter than desired." This is general context that could relate to stock levels in the flagged categories.

plan.why: The three departments with the largest dollar gaps (Health & Beauty, Home Storage, and Dry Grocery) are the ones where searches for category, quarter, and regional explanations can most plausibly support the flagged drops.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

This was an 11.3 percent increase from the $0.97 per share reported for the third quarter last year.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Doug is up next with an International update. Doug…
passages.text: Turning to Japan…After a strong first half, our business is experiencing additional challenges from the broader macroeconomic environment in the country. Simply, consumer sentiment is weakening. We continue to outperform the market in comp store sales through the strength of EDLP and the price gap that we've created over the last couple of years. Walmart Japan's net sales and comp sales were down 1.8 and 1.9 percent, respectively. Third quarter average ticket was down 0.2 percent and traffic was down 1.7 percent. According to statistics released by the Japanese Ministry of the Economy, Trade and Industry, or METI, overall supermarket comparable sales for the third quarter declined by 2.5 percent, indicating that Walmart continues to outperform the market.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Health & wellness continued its trend, generating a low single-digit positive comp. Over the counter remained very strong as our broad assortment and continued focus on opening price point drove traffic gains and unit growth. Customers are finding value in our broader assortment of active nutrition products like whey protein and meal supplement bars. As expected, brand to generic conversions continued to pressure top-line sales, but conversions of Lipitor and other brands continue to improve pharmacy margins.

Retail and Tourism First District retail contacts offer a very mixed take on economic conditions in the region. Demand remains strong for adult clothing, but spending on durable items such as furniture and electronics continues to be lower than earlier in the year. Some companies cite disappointing sales during the last six weeks, while others report some upside surprises. Sales results range from low single-digit declines to high single-digit increases compared with a year earlier. Some contacts say that consumer sentiment has become more negative, while others observe that consumers are "coming back." Retailers note wholesale prices remain flat so they are holding selling prices steady. Respondents still express uncertainty about the direction of the U.S. economy and say they expect little improvement over the next six to eight months.

report.summary: For the week ending Sep 14, 2012, Store 23 was below the ML forecast in 57 of its 67 departments, and the store as a whole was $1,277,761 against a $1,421,143 forecast. The same departments were also down at most other stores, which points to a wider pattern rather than something only at this store. The reports give only general context, and no store-side cause was found in the data.

findings.title: Walmart-wide week also below forecast
findings.text: All 45 Walmart stores together were $44,169,616 against a $46,628,419 forecast that week, and 36 of 45 stores were below forecast. This is a broad dip, not one specific to Store 23.

findings.title: Same departments down at most other stores
findings.text: Paper Goods was below forecast at 42 of 44 other stores, and Stationery at 43 of 44. Health & Beauty Aids was below forecast at 40 of 44 other stores. These departments fell across the chain, not only here.

findings.title: Store-wide shortfall across most departments
findings.text: Store 23 was below forecast in 57 of its 67 departments, and the store as a whole was 10.1% below forecast. That is a larger gap than the Walmart-wide 5.3% drop, so the shortfall spread across many departments here.

findings.title: Outside factors show only small changes
findings.text: The week had no holiday. Fuel was $3.99/gal against $3.88 before, temperature was 61°F against 68°F, and unemployment was 4.2%, the same as before. These changes are small or general, and none points to a specific department.

findings.title: Boston district reported weaker durable sales
findings.text: The Boston Fed's Aug 29, 2012 report said "spending on durable items such as furniture and electronics continues to be lower than earlier in the year." This is for the district as a whole and predates the week, so it is only general context for Furniture and Electronics.

departments.what_supports_it: Actual sales were $68,404 against a $78,787 ML forecast, 13.2% below. Five other New England stores were also below forecast in this department, and 40 of 44 other stores were too, so the drop is shared.
Actual sales were $38,768 against a $47,527 ML forecast, 18.4% below. 42 of 44 other stores were below forecast in this department, with a median of -16.0%, so the drop was widespread.
Actual sales were $67,507 against a $75,845 ML forecast, 11.0% below. Other stores were close to forecast overall (median -0.9%), so this department's gap is larger here than elsewhere.
Actual sales were $54,726 against a $62,637 ML forecast, 12.6% below. 37 of 44 other stores were below forecast, and all 5 New England stores were too.

Actual sales were $61,863 against a $69,437 ML forecast, 10.9% below. Other stores were close to forecast (median +0.0%), and Walmart's earnings call said "Over the counter remained very strong," so this department's gap is harder to explain with the wider pattern.

report.not_found: No store-side cause such as a stock shortage, staffing change, local competitor or local event was in the data, and no holiday or major weather shift was found that would explain the drop.
next_steps: Check stock on hand and recent deliveries for Health & Beauty Aids, Home Management / Storage and Dry Grocery.
Check staffing and shift coverage for the week ending Sep 14, 2012.
Check pricing and display changes in the flagged departments that week.
Check for local events, road works or competitor openings near Store 23 that week.
Check that the week's department sales were entered correctly.
data_needed: Store-level inventory on hand and delivery records by department for the week
Staffing schedules and hours for the week
Pricing and display change logs by department
Local competitor and event records for the store's area
Department-level markdown records (only store-level markdowns are available, so these cannot be tied to a department)

passages.text: Consumer Spending Consumer spending improved with stronger than expected sales in June and was expected to strengthen further in the coming months. District retailers reported increased sales, particularly for seasonal items, mid-priced appliances, apparel, and fashion accessories. Several high-end retailers, however, commented that economic uncertainty had slowed demand for luxury items. Auto sales climbed sharply and were expected to remain solid for the next few months with more dealers offering sales incentives and discounts. Fuel-efficient cars sold well, while demand for large, expensive cars and trucks remained weak. Restaurant sales increased more than expected as both the number of diners and average check amounts edged up in June. Tourism activity ramped up with the start of the summer vacation season, though wildfires in Colorado hurt traffic in the Rocky Mountain region. District hotel owners reported a sharp rise in occupancy at higher average room rates and expected bookings to remain strong during the next three months.

passages.text: Grocery, which includes food and consumables, delivered a low single-digit positive comp for the quarter. The program has helped drive sales to the entire meat department, which outperformed the overall food business by approximately 300 basis points in the second quarter. The unmatched combination of quality and value has resonated with a large number of our customers, including many who had not previously shopped our meat department.

report.summary: Store 13 was below the ML forecast in 17 flagged departments, a total of $101,263 (an ML estimate, not a verified loss). The same departments were also below forecast at most other stores that week, and the whole chain was below forecast too, so the pattern looks broader than this store alone. No report or store record explained the gaps for these departments.

findings.title: Chain-wide sales were below forecast
findings.text: Across all 45 stores that week, sales were $44,084,063 against a $46,419,912 forecast (-5.0%), and 43 of 45 stores were below forecast. Store 13 was -6.9% overall, with 61 of 70 departments below forecast.

findings.title: Same departments down at many stores
findings.text: In Dept 95 DSD Grocery, Snacks & Beverages, 39 of 44 other stores were below forecast that week. In Dept 93 Meat, 36 of 41 were below, and in Dept 5 Media & Gaming, 37 of 44 were below. This suggests a shared cause across stores rather than a problem only at this store.

findings.title: Some gaps larger than other stores
findings.text: Store 13's drops in Dept 25 Shoes (-22.5%), Dept 95 DSD Grocery, Snacks & Beverages (-11.0%) and Dept 93 Meat (-13.4%) were larger than the typical store's drops in those departments (medians of -11.0%, -5.3% and -10.1%). A local factor may be part of the reason, but none was found in the data.

findings.title: Regional traffic report from Colorado wildfires
findings.text: A Federal Reserve Beige Book from Jul 18, 2012 said "wildfires in Colorado hurt traffic in the Rocky Mountain region." The report covers the Kansas City Fed district as a whole and does not mention Store 13 or the week ending Jul 27, 2012. It also said district retailers reported increased sales in apparel, so it does not explain the apparel drops.

findings.title: Outside factors changed little
findings.text: There was no holiday that week. Local fuel was $3.54 per gallon against $3.61 before, temperature was 80°F against 81°F, and unemployment was 5.8% in both periods. None of these is a large change that would clearly explain a drop.

findings.title: Store-wide markdowns cannot be tied to departments
findings.text: The store recorded $22,175 in markdowns across 5 fields this week. These are recorded for the whole store only and cannot be linked to any department, so they cannot explain the department drops.

departments.what_supports_it: 39 of 44 other stores were also below forecast in this department that week, with a median of -5.3%. Store 13 was -11.0%, and both other Rocky Mountain stores were also below forecast.
36 of 41 other stores were below forecast, with a median of -10.1%. Store 13 was -13.4%, and both other Rocky Mountain stores were also below forecast.
38 of 42 other stores were below forecast, with a median of -11.0%. Store 13's -22.5% is one of the larger gaps in the data, but no store-side reason was found.
37 of 44 other stores were below forecast, with a median of -13.6%. Store 13 was -13.9%, close to the typical gap, and both other Rocky Mountain stores were also below forecast.
40 of 44 other stores were below forecast, with a median of -12.3%. Store 13 was -9.3%, close to the typical gap.

report.not_found: No store-specific event, stock or delivery record, staffing note, or competitor report was found, and no report named Store 13 or this week.
next_steps: Check stock on hand and recent deliveries for Snacks & Beverages, Meat and Shoes that week.
Check whether staffing in these departments was short that week.
Check any price changes, displays or promotions in these departments that week.
Check for local events, store closures or new competitors near the store that week.
Check that the week's sales were recorded correctly for these departments.

Staffing schedules for the affected departments
Price change and display logs for the affected departments
A list of local events and competitor openings near the store
Department-level markdown records (currently only store-level totals exist)

findings.title: Same departments down at most stores
findings.text: Stationery was below forecast at 43 of 44 other stores, and Girlswear at 33 of 36. Boyswear was below forecast at 28 of 36 other stores, so the drops in these departments are not unique to Store 24.

findings.title: Apparel drops seen across New York stores
findings.text: Girlswear, Boyswear, Menswear and Shoes were below forecast at all three other New York State stores in the data. This suggests a regional or category pattern, but the cause is not identified.

findings.title: Store-wide markdowns cannot be tied to departments
findings.text: Store 24 recorded $13,404 in markdowns across the whole store that week. These markdowns cannot be linked to any one department, so they cannot be used to explain the department drops.

findings.title: Outside factors only modestly different
findings.text: There was no holiday that week. Fuel was $4.09/gal against $4.01, temperature was 64°F against 72°F, and unemployment was 9.0% against 9.0%. Lower temperatures could affect some categories, but nothing in the data links them to these departments.

findings.title: Report context: apparel prices steady
findings.text: The Aug 29, 2012 Beige Book says "Retail prices continue to be described as steady--including apparel prices." It also says "sales activity has firmed somewhat since the last report." That report predates the Sep 14, 2012 week and does not cover it.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Those forward- looking statements also include statements of management's expectations: for the Walmart U.S. segment's stores being the number one holiday destination in fiscal 2013; that the segment will recognize most of the $300 million of additional layaway sales made in the quarter ended October 31, 2012, in the quarter ending January 31, 2013 when customers pay for and pick up the merchandise; for the number of store openings in the quarter ending January 31, 2013; that certain initiatives will help the segment reach its savings goal in fiscal 2013 and the future; for the segment's plans for Black Friday; for the number of impressions across social media the segment will generate in the fiscal 2013 holiday season; that the segment will have a strong performance through Thanksgiving and Black Friday; and that the segment will continue to deliver consistent core growth.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

• Health and wellness includes pharmacy, optical services and over-the-counter drugs. The percentage of net sales for the Sam's Club segment, including online sales, by merchandise category, was as follows for fiscal 2013, 2012 and 2011: Fiscal Years Ended January 31, MERCHANDISE CATEGORY 2013 2012 2011 Grocery and consumables 55% 55% 55%

Similarly, weekly attendance and revenues at Broadway theaters were running ahead of comparable 2011 levels in August and early September but slipped well below year-earlier levels for the third week of the month. Finally, consumer confidence fell in August and was little changed at a low level in September, according to the Conference Board's monthly survey of residents of the Middle Atlantic states (NY, NJ, Pa).

report.summary: Store 24 ran further below its ML forecast than the chain did that week: $1,255,415 against $1,383,004 (-9.2%), compared with -2.6% for all 45 stores. Most New York stores were also below forecast in the same departments, and a Fed report describes New York retail sales as "flat to softer," so regional softness is a possible contributor. The reasons for this store's larger gaps are not established by the data.

findings.title: Store fell further than the chain
findings.text: The store as a whole was $1,255,415 against a $1,383,004 forecast (-9.2%). Across all 45 stores, sales were $44,957,207 against $46,148,335 (-2.6%), and 33 of 45 stores were below forecast that week.

findings.title: Regional softness in New York
findings.text: The Oct 10, 2012 Beige Book says retail sales were "flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts." This is a district-wide description, not a finding about this store.

findings.title: Grocery drops shared across New York stores
findings.text: Dry Grocery, DSD Grocery, Snacks & Beverages and Frozen Food were below forecast at all three other New York stores that week. Store 24's gaps in these departments were larger than the New York median in most cases.

findings.title: Pharmacy drop not matched chain-wide
findings.text: Walmart's earnings call described health and wellness as having "a low single-digit positive comp" and said "brand to generic conversions continued to pressure top-line sales." The call does not describe this store's pharmacy drop, and no store-side pharmacy data was provided.

findings.title: Weather and fuel changed only slightly
findings.text: The week had no holiday. Temperature was 53°F against 60°F in the prior four-week median, fuel was $4.15/gal against $4.17, and unemployment was 8.7% against 8.8%. None of these was linked in the data to specific departments.

departments.what_supports_it: Actual $126,125 against a $134,807 ML forecast (-6.4%). All three other New York stores were also below forecast (Store 15 -5.2%; Store 19 -4.9%; Store 27 -3.2%), but across all stores the median was -1.2%.

Actual $21,571 against $29,368 (-26.5%). Across all stores the median was -5.2%, and in New York only Store 27 was below forecast (-5.4%), while Store 15 was +28.6%, so the drop looks specific to this store.
Actual $9,892 against $14,739 (-32.9%), the largest percentage gap in the flagged list. Two of three New York stores were below forecast (Store 27 -9.5%; Store 19 -3.0%), and Store 15 was +4.2%.

Actual $51,052 against $58,519 (-12.8%). Two of three New York stores were below forecast (Store 19 -2.2%; Store 27 -1.7%), but across all stores the median was -1.6%, and the Walmart call described pharmacy as pressured by brand-to-generic conversions.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Most of our merchandising areas again delivered solid performance, though industry trends in electronics continue to impact the broader entertainment category. We're seeing market share growth across grocery and health & wellness. You can expect to hear more about market share and how we're using Nielsen data during our annual analyst meeting in October.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.text: So, let's cover our reported results, which include fuel sales. Net sales were $13.9 billion, a 4.7 percent increase over last year's third quarter. Fuel prices were up 6.0 percent compared to last year and gallons sold were up 7.2 percent, thus creating a boost to overall sales of 1.1 percent. Gross profit rate was down 5 basis points. Operating expenses as a percentage of net sales decreased by 31 basis points. Operating income increased 12.7 percent to $435 million.

Consumer Spending Retailers report that sales activity has firmed somewhat since the last report. Two major retail chains report that sales in the region were on plan in July and ahead of plan in early August. Similarly a major retail mall in upstate New York reports some firming in sales, as well as shopper traffic, in July and early August, following lackluster business in May and June. Retail prices continue to be described as steady--including apparel prices, which had previously been expected to drift down with the retreat in cotton prices earlier this year. Stores in New York City have performed on par or modestly better than those in the rest of the region. Inventories are generally said to be at or slightly above desired levels.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.text: A few reminders before we get into the details: Walmart's consolidated financial statements are based on a fiscal year ending January 31 for both our U.S. and Canadian operations, and December 31 for all other operations. We provide comparable sales guidance for Walmart U.S. and Sam's Club on the 4-5-4 calendar each quarter for the upcoming quarter. We do not give any annual comp guidance for the U.S. operations.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Health and wellness continues to be a key traffic driver as well and overall delivered a mid single-digit comp increase. Hearing aid centers achieved double-digit comps for the quarter. We had mid single-digit comps in OTC and low single-digit comps in prescriptions. Like Walmart U.S., the recent availability of popular prescriptions that have moved from branded to generic status negatively impacted overall sales, but drove profitability and unit volume. Rx script count was up mid single-digits, and we expect this trend to continue.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

• Health and wellness includes pharmacy, optical services and over-the-counter drugs. The percentage of net sales for the Sam's Club segment, including online sales, by merchandise category, was as follows for fiscal 2013, 2012 and 2011: Fiscal Years Ended January 31, MERCHANDISE CATEGORY 2013 2012 2011 Grocery and consumables 55% 55% 55%

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported modest increases in retail spending on a year-over-year basis, but many reported slower growth in recent months compared with earlier in the year; however, Boston and Cleveland reported sales as flat, and New York cited softer sales. There were a few reports that high summer temperatures negatively affected sales. Sales of big-ticket household goods were strong in the Richmond, Chicago, Kansas City, and Dallas Districts, while sales were reportedly flat for home furnishings and major appliances in the San Francisco District. Boston reported that sales for furniture and electronics had slowed, and retailers in the New York District reported that home goods sales were weak. Reports from luxury-goods retailers were mixed.

Retail and Tourism First District retail contacts offer a very mixed take on economic conditions in the region. Demand remains strong for adult clothing, but spending on durable items such as furniture and electronics continues to be lower than earlier in the year. Some companies cite disappointing sales during the last six weeks, while others report some upside surprises. Sales results range from low single-digit declines to high single-digit increases compared with a year earlier. Some contacts say that consumer sentiment has become more negative, while others observe that consumers are "coming back." Retailers note wholesale prices remain flat so they are holding selling prices steady. Respondents still express uncertainty about the direction of the U.S. economy and say they expect little improvement over the next six to eight months.

findings.title: Durable goods and weather context

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Comp sales in technology and entertainment, which continued to experience deflation, were slightly positive this quarter. Wireless, up double-digit comps, performed well and benefitted from both the Samsung Galaxy III and the Apple iPhone 5. Televisions and home theater comps are up low single-digit, driven by unit movement and improved availability in large screen televisions. Average selling prices continue to decrease for TVs, and our inventory position for the holidays is very good. Video games, music and movies continue to experience pressure in the current environment.

Retail Sales Retail sales growth softened over the reporting period, and sales are up slightly year-over-year. Sales in the Eleventh District continue to outperform the nation, according to two national retailers. Contacts noted that holiday hiring has begun or will begin soon, and hours worked are up from the previous report. Commodity input costs are easing, but the drought has caused prices for grains and feedstock to rise. The outlook for the rest of the retail quarter, which ends in October, is mixed but contacts are cautiously optimistic for the fourth quarter.

passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: We're so excited about our annual Black Friday event and how it will drive sales throughout the entire holiday season. Our customers asked for an earlier start time, so this year the event begins at 8:00 p.m. on Thursday. The first event will have unbeatable deals for the entire family in key areas like toys, gaming, home and apparel. At 10:00 p.m. we'll highlight special deals in electronics that will excite our customers, and let me point out that we're far deeper in the quantities of those items than we've ever been before. We'll continue through Friday and into the weekend with more great prices on key gift items across the entire store.

These reclassifications did not impact the Company's consolidated operating income or net income. Additionally, certain prior period segment asset and expense allocations have been reclassified among segments to be comparable with the current period presentation. The Retail Industry We operate in the highly competitive retail industry in all of the countries we serve. We face strong sales competition from other discount, department, drug, dollar, variety and specialty stores, warehouse clubs and supermarkets. Many of these competitors are national, regional or international chains, as well as internet-based retailers and catalog businesses.

The Eleventh District economy expanded at a moderate pace over the past six weeks. Energy activity remained strong, and construction and real estate activity picked up as housing demand strengthened. Demand for business services improved slightly, and transportation services activity continued to expand. Reports on manufacturing activity were mixed. Growth in retail and auto sales slowed over the reporting period, but Eleventh District sales continued to outperform the national average, according to respondents. Lenders noted steady loan demand. Agricultural conditions improved slightly. Price and wage pressures were modest over the reporting period, and employment levels continued to edge up. Many respondents across industries said continued uncertainty about upcoming elections was clouding outlooks.

report.summary: Store 11 was below the ML forecast in 60 of its 69 departments for the week ending Oct 19, 2012, a larger gap than Walmart overall that week. Electronics and infant apparel were below the forecast at most stores in the region, which points toward a shared category or regional cause, while Toys looks more local to this store. These are possible reasons only, and the data does not confirm any of them.

findings.title: Electronics below forecast at many stores
findings.text: Dept 72 Electronics was below the ML forecast at 33 of 41 other stores that week, and 9 of 13 other Texas stores were below it too. Walmart's report also describes entertainment as experiencing deflation, with "Video games, music and movies continue to experience pressure in the current environment."

findings.title: Infant apparel below forecast across Texas
findings.text: Dept 26 Infant Apparel was below the ML forecast at 29 of 39 other stores, and all 10 other Texas stores were below it too. This pattern suggests a shared regional or category factor rather than something only at this store.

findings.title: Store well below Walmart's overall trend
findings.text: Walmart as a whole that week was $44,957,207 against a $46,148,335 forecast (-2.6%), with 33 of 45 stores below. Store 11 was $1,232,035 against $1,356,196 (-9.2%), so its shortfall is larger than the overall pattern.

findings.title: Toys drop mostly at this store
findings.text: Dept 7 Toys was $11,825 below the ML forecast here (-30.3%), but across all stores the department was roughly on forecast (all together +0.4%). Only 26 of 44 other stores were below it, so this drop looks more local than shared.

findings.title: Regional sales growth softened, per Fed
findings.text: The Dallas Fed Beige Book of Oct 10, 2012 says "Retail sales growth softened over the reporting period." This describes the Eleventh District as a whole, not this store, and it is general context only.

findings.title: Calendar and local conditions mostly unchanged
findings.text: No holiday fell in this week. Fuel was $3.59/gal against $3.64, temperature was 74°F against 74°F, and unemployment was 6.0% against 6.2%, so these outside factors do not clearly explain the gap.

plan.why: The three departments with the largest dollar gaps (Dry Grocery, DSD Snacks & Beverages, and Meat) are all grocery-driven, so the searches focus on grocery demand, Walmart's quarter, and regional fuel and spending pressure that week.

passages.text: During the 13-week period, both comp ticket and traffic rose for Walmart U.S., and both grocery and general merchandise had positive comp sales. "Our comp sales momentum continued through the second quarter, with July being one of our strongest months. All three geographic business units and all store formats had positive comp sales. Customers are responding to our continued focus on providing the right assortment at everyday low prices and are shopping the entire store," said Bill Simon, Walmart U.S. president and chief executive officer. "We have a powerful strategy and I'm confident in our ability to deliver sustained strong financial performance." For the 4-5-4 period from July 28 through October 26, Walmart U.S. expects comparable store sales to range from 1.0 percent to 3.0 percent.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Consumer Spending Retailers report that sales activity has firmed somewhat since the last report. Two major retail chains report that sales in the region were on plan in July and ahead of plan in early August. Similarly a major retail mall in upstate New York reports some firming in sales, as well as shopper traffic, in July and early August, following lackluster business in May and June. Retail prices continue to be described as steady--including apparel prices, which had previously been expected to drift down with the retreat in cotton prices earlier this year. Stores in New York City have performed on par or modestly better than those in the rest of the region. Inventories are generally said to be at or slightly above desired levels.

(Walmart) reported second quarter diluted earnings per share from continuing operations of $1.18, at the top of our guidance of $1.13 to $1.18. This was an 8.3 percent increase from the $1.09 per share reported for the second quarter last year.

Large areas of the mid-Atlantic lost power for up to a week following strong storms at the end of June; a retailer in the Richmond area reported having to place extra orders for generators as his stock depleted. He noted that bottled water sold out quickly, and sales of battery operated lights and flashlights rose sharply. Retail prices increased at a somewhat faster pace since our last report.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Now, I'll turn it over to Doug for the International update. Doug …
passages.text: Despite a difficult consumer environment and the wettest weather on record, ASDA gained market share in the second quarter, according to the Kantar Worldwide Panel Total Till Roll for the 12 weeks ending July 8. Excluding fuel, net sales grew 3.2 percent. Comparable sales, excluding fuel, increased 0.7 percent, with ticket up 2.6 percent, and traffic decreasing 1.9 percent. The strongest performances were in grocery, apparel and electronics. In addition, our online business in the U.K. improved its already strong performance, with sales growth of 22.1 percent in the quarter.

passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: We had positive comps across all geographies and store formats. During the quarter, we focused on being the destination for back-to-school and Halloween shopping. Our merchants and operators developed a strong cross-functional plan, and I'm pleased with our execution and the sales growth achieved this year. As a reminder, a slightly larger portion of Halloween sales versus last year will fall into the fourth quarter comp period, given how the 4-5-4 calendar falls this year.

The price of WTI rose during the reporting period, reaching nearly $99 per barrel. Natural gas prices remained depressed. Retail and on-highway prices of both gasoline and diesel ended the reporting period slightly higher. Contacts noted that Hurricane Isaac had little impact on energy pricing. The prices of petrochemical products were flat to slightly up over the past six weeks.
